subject.title: Per-account native command prefix for multi-agent slash commands

question: Should Slack multi-account native slash commands be solved with validated account-level nativeNames mapping, constrained nativePrefix sugar, or documented as unsupported for duplicate native command names?
rationale: Current main has no account-level naming contract, and the two prior unmerged PRs show a real design fork between prefix convenience and explicit mappings; adding either path expands Slack config/API surface.

options.title: Implement validated nativeNames
options.body: Add one explicit per-account mapping surface with duplicate/format validation, registration and reverse lookup support, docs, and tests; this matches the later PR direction and avoids implicit prefix aliases.

options.title: Implement constrained nativePrefix
options.body: Add prefix sugar only with strict lowercase/slug validation and no broad dash-stripping fallback, accepting a simpler UX but a second naming abstraction.

options.title: Document unsupported duplicate names
options.body: Leave runtime unchanged and document that multiple Slack apps in one workspace must not register identical native command names, preserving current config surface at the cost of the reported multi-agent workflow.

recommendation.title: Implement validated nativeNames
recommendation.body: Add one explicit per-account mapping surface with duplicate/format validation, registration and reverse lookup support, docs, and tests; this matches the later PR direction and avoids implicit prefix aliases.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant current and historical code trail for Slack native commands and shared command registry behavior points to steipete.
